overview.title: The world of the first Christians
overview.intro: The places that matter most in this era, from Jerusalem to Rome. Region names are the Roman ones used in Acts and Paul's letters.

journey-1.title: First journey
journey-1.intro: Acts says the church at Antioch sent out Barnabas and Paul. They crossed Cyprus, then went inland to cities in the Roman province of Galatia, in the regions Acts calls Pisidia and Lycaonia, and came back the same way.

stops.name: Antioch
stops.note: Barnabas and Saul are sent out

journey-2.title: Second journey
journey-2.intro: Acts says Paul set out again with Silas, revisited the churches inland, then crossed by sea into Macedonia and Greece for the first time.

stops.name: Troas
stops.note: A vision of a man of Macedonia

stops.name: Caesarea
stops.note: He lands, then goes up to greet the church

journey-3.title: Third journey
journey-3.intro: Acts says Paul spent a long stay in Ephesus, went back through Macedonia and Greece, then sailed down the coast toward Jerusalem.

stops.name: Antioch
stops.note: Paul sets out through Galatia and Phrygia

stops.name: Ephesus
stops.note: About two to three years; a riot

stops.name: Philippi
stops.note: After the days of Unleavened Bread

voyage.title: Voyage to Rome
voyage.intro: Acts says Paul, now a prisoner, was sent to Rome by ship. A storm drove the ship west for two weeks until it wrecked on Malta.

stops.name: Caesarea
stops.note: Paul is handed to a centurion

stops.name: Myra
stops.note: They change to a ship of Alexandria

stops.name: Malta
stops.note: Shipwreck; three months on the island

stops.name: Rome
stops.note: Two years under guard, still teaching

churches.title: Cities named in the sources for this era
churches.intro: The cities that appear most often in the writings of AD 100 to 313, from Antioch in the east to Carthage in the west. Lyons and Vienne in Gaul, where Irenaeus was bishop, lie off the western edge of this map.

ignatius.title: Ignatius on the road to Rome
ignatius.intro: Eusebius says Ignatius was sent from Syria to Rome under military guard, and that he wrote from Smyrna and from Troas. Polycarp's letter shows the Philippians had seen him pass. Nothing records the rest of the way, so the lines between these stops are straight and show only the order.

stops.name: Antioch
stops.note: Ignatius is bishop here and is sent to Rome

stops.name: Smyrna
stops.note: He meets Polycarp and writes to Ephesus, Magnesia, Tralles and Rome

stops.name: Troas
stops.note: He writes to Philadelphia, Smyrna and Polycarp

stops.name: Philippi
stops.note: Polycarp says the Philippians saw Ignatius, Rufus and Zosimus

stops.name: Rome
stops.note: He writes that he expects to face wild beasts here

church-around-400.title: The church around AD 400
church-around-400.intro: The main churches and cities of the empire around the time of the councils of the fourth century. Boundaries are simplified.

churches-about-600.title: Churches and kingdoms about 600
churches-about-600.intro: The churches in the era of Gregory the Great and Justinian: Rome and Ravenna, the eastern patriarchates, Carthage, and the new English church. Boundaries are simplified.

english-and-east-700.title: The English church and the East, about 700
english-and-east-700.intro: Whitby, Lindisfarne and Canterbury in the north and west, with the eastern cities of the councils. Boundaries are simplified.

carolingian-world.title: The Carolingian world and the schism
carolingian-world.intro: The Frankish kingdoms around Aachen and Verdun, the papacy in Rome, and the eastern and northern frontiers. Boundaries are simplified.

crusades-and-reform.title: Reform and crusade, about 1100
crusades-and-reform.intro: The reforming papacy and its opponents, the monasteries of Cluny and Cîteaux, and the road to Jerusalem. Boundaries are simplified.

schism-and-councils.title: The schism and the councils
schism-and-councils.intro: Avignon and Rome, the councils of Constance and Basel, and the frontier with the Ottomans at Kosovo. Boundaries are simplified.

late-medieval-europe.title: Europe in the fifteenth century
late-medieval-europe.intro: The councils of Basel and Florence, the Renaissance courts of Italy, Constantinople and the Ottoman frontier in the Balkans, and the edge of Muscovy. Boundaries are simplified.

religion-1555.title: Religion in Europe about 1555
religion-1555.intro: After the Peace of Augsburg, the German princes chose their religion, and the Reformed churches held Geneva, Scotland and parts of the Netherlands. Boundaries are simplified.

thirty-years-war.title: The Thirty Years' War, 1618 to 1648
thirty-years-war.intro: The war began in Bohemia and spread across the empire, drawing in Denmark, Sweden and France. Westphalia, where the peace was made, is shown in the north-west. Boundaries are simplified.

confessions-1700.title: Confessions in Europe about 1700
confessions-1700.intro: Catholic, Lutheran, Reformed and Orthodox lands after the wars of religion, with the Habsburg and Ottoman frontiers. Boundaries are simplified.

europe-1789.title: Europe in 1789
europe-1789.intro: The states of Europe on the eve of the French Revolution: the Estates-General at Versailles, the Habsburg and Prussian courts, the Russian Holy Synod, and the Jesuit suppression. Boundaries are simplified.

europe-1815.title: Europe after the Congress of Vienna, 1815
europe-1815.intro: The restored states of Europe, with the Papal States returned to the pope and the Holy Alliance in place. Boundaries are simplified.

papal-states-1789-1870.title: The Papal States, 1789 to 1870
papal-states-1789-1870.intro: Rome and its territory in the years between the Revolution and the fall of Rome. The papal enclaves in France (Avignon and the Venaissin) were lost in 1790 and the Papal States were occupied in 1809 and again in 1860 and 1870. Boundaries are simplified and approximate.

balkans-1821-1870.title: The Balkans and the Ottoman East, 1821 to 1870
balkans-1821-1870.intro: Greece, the Danubian principalities, the Bulgarian Exarchate of 1870, and the Ottoman capital. Boundaries are simplified.

ottoman-balkans-1878.title: The Ottoman Balkans and the Congress of Berlin, 1878
ottoman-balkans-1878.intro: The Balkans and eastern Anatolia after the Russo-Turkish war, as settled at the Congress of Berlin. Boundaries are simplified and approximate.

europe-1914.title: Europe in 1914
europe-1914.intro: The great powers on the eve of the First World War, with the Ottoman lands and the Armenian provinces. Boundaries are simplified.

europe-1933-1945.title: Europe, 1933 to 1945
europe-1933-1945.intro: Germany, Italy, Spain and the Soviet Union, with the places where the churches met the regimes: Rome, Berlin, Barmen and Flossenbürg. Boundaries are simplified.

europe-divided-1950.title: Europe divided, 1950
europe-divided-1950.intro: The Iron Curtain across Europe in 1950, with the Soviet-controlled churches to the east and the free churches to the west. Boundaries are simplified.

central-europe-1956-1989.title: Central and Eastern Europe, 1956 to 1989
central-europe-1956-1989.intro: The churches of the Soviet bloc and their neighbours, from the Hungarian uprising of 1956 to the revolutions of 1989. Boundaries are simplified.

first-crusade-1096-1099.title: The First Crusade, 1096 to 1099
first-crusade-1096-1099.intro: The route of the crusading armies from Constantinople to Jerusalem, with the battles and sieges that marked it. The route is simplified and straight between places; the battle sites and dates are not yet checked.

stops.name: Nicaea
stops.note: Besieged from May 1097 and surrendered in June to the Byzantine emperor, not to the crusaders

stops.name: Dorylaeum
stops.note: Battle in July 1097, where the crusaders defeat the Seljuk army after a surprise attack

stops.name: Antioch
stops.note: Siege from October 1097; the city is taken in June 1098 and the army is then besieged inside it

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.note: Captured on 15 July 1099 after a siege; the chroniclers describe the killing that followed

stops.name: Ascalon
stops.note: Battle in August 1099, where the crusaders defeat the Fatimid army
